high.title: USD Price Increases to Maximum Limit, Free Market Exceeds 27,000 VND/USD
high.summary: The Vietnamese dong has weakened significantly against the USD amid Middle East geopolitical tensions. The State Bank of Vietnam set the central rate at 25,059 VND/USD (up 2 VND), while commercial banks are quoting USD at maximum allowed rates of 26,311 VND/USD for selling. Notably, buying rates have surged dramatically - Vietcombank increased buying rates by 40 VND to 26,041 VND/USD, while VietinBank raised it by 57 VND. The free market rate has broken above 27,000 VND/USD. This reflects strong USD demand driven by global risk-off sentiment from Middle East conflicts, with oil prices rising 8-13% in recent days. The SBV Deputy Governor noted this creates inflationary pressure and makes central banks globally more cautious about rate cuts, potentially leading to tighter monetary policy ahead.

high.title: How Middle East Tensions Impact USD Prices
high.summary: USD/VND rates continue rising with the central rate now at 25,057 VND/USD, up 13 VND over the past week. Commercial banks quote around 26,029-26,309 VND/USD while free market rates hit 26,850-26,880 VND/USD. This reflects global USD strength amid heightened geopolitical risks. The SBV Deputy Governor warns that Middle East escalation has driven oil prices up 8-13% in days, creating inflationary pressure globally. Many major central banks are now more cautious about rate cuts, with some potentially raising rates. For Vietnam, this external pressure complicates monetary policy as imported inflation through energy costs could force the SBV to prioritize price stability over growth support, potentially limiting room for accommodative policies.

high.title: USD and Oil Prices Surge Due to Middle East Conflict: How Will Exchange Rates and Inflation in Vietnam Be Affected?
high.summary: The US-Israel military action against Iran has triggered immediate global financial market reactions. The USD Index jumped 0.8% to 98.42 points while gold prices also surged, reflecting clear "risk-off" sentiment. Vietcombank Securities (VCBS) notes that in this uncertain geopolitical environment, global capital flows are being reallocated toward safe-haven assets. For Vietnam's economy, this creates multiple transmission channels: higher energy import costs (Vietnam imports ~85% of oil needs), potential VND depreciation pressure requiring SBV intervention, and imported inflation that could force tighter monetary policy. The analysis suggests Vietnam's inflation target of 4.5% for 2026 faces significant upward pressure, potentially constraining the SBV's ability to support growth through loose monetary policy.

high.title: Urgent: Proposal to Reduce Import Tariffs on Gasoline and Oil to 0%
high.summary: The Ministry of Finance is building a decree to reduce preferential import tariffs (MFN) to 0% for certain gasoline, oil, and input materials. The proposal has been sent to the Ministry of Justice for review. The war between the US, Israel and Iran has severely affected petroleum business in Vietnam and globally. Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz prevents about 20 million barrels of crude oil daily from Middle Eastern sources from reaching refineries worldwide, especially in Asia. This has forced Asian refineries to cut capacity, open strategic reserves, and limit/stop petroleum product exports, creating severe supply shortages and pushing Singapore market prices (both Mops and Pre) extremely high. This mirrors similar emergency tariff measures taken during past oil crises and represents a critical policy tool to stabilize domestic fuel supplies.

high.title: Reduce Import Tariffs on Some Gasoline and Oil Products to 0%
high.summary: The Government has issued Decree 72/2026/ND-CP amending preferential import tax rates for gasoline, oil, and production materials to 0%. This responds to Middle East tensions, particularly the US-Israel-Iran conflict affecting global energy markets and Strait of Hormuz shipping routes that carry crucial Middle Eastern crude oil. The disruption directly impacts Asia, which heavily depends on Middle Eastern crude. The decree aims to help businesses secure import sources and stabilize domestic fuel supply. This represents emergency fiscal policy to counter external energy shocks and maintain price stability in Vietnam's economy.

high.title: G7 Just Made Emergency Move to Protect Supply, Oil Prices Immediately Drop $15 in Under 2 Hours
high.summary: US crude oil prices dropped $15/barrel in under two hours after reports that G7 countries are considering releasing 300-400 million barrels from strategic petroleum reserves to stabilize global energy markets. WTI crude now trades below $104/barrel after the sharp decline. This emergency coordinated response aims to reduce price pressure amid supply disruption fears from Middle East geopolitical tensions. Previously, oil had surged over 25% to above $110/barrel - the highest since mid-2022 during the Russia-Ukraine conflict. The week saw crude oil rise about 35%, marking the largest weekly gain in recent history. This G7 intervention demonstrates major economies' commitment to preventing an energy crisis that could derail global economic recovery.

medium.title: VN-Index Lost Over 113 Points in 1 Week, Experts Name Stock Groups in "Oversold Zone"
medium.summary: Vietnam's stock market closed the first week of March negatively with VN-Index falling sharply to 1,767 points, losing over 40 points in the final session and over 113 points for the week. The decline resembles the "tariff shock" from April 2025, driven by escalating Middle East geopolitical tensions that have worried investors significantly.

medium.title: BIDV Bank Interest Rates March 2025: Which Term Has the Highest Interest Rate?
medium.summary: BIDV maintains stable deposit rates in March 2026, with counter deposits at 0.1% for demand deposits, rising to 5.3% for 24-36 month terms - the highest rates offered. The 12-month term offers 5.2% annually, positioning BIDV competitively in the current interest rate environment.

medium.title: MB Bank Just Increased Savings Interest Rates Significantly
medium.summary: Military Bank (MB) has raised deposit rates substantially for terms over 12 months while keeping shorter terms unchanged. The 12-18 month rates increased from 5.5% to 6.1% (up 0.6pp), while 24-60 month terms rose from 6.3% to 6.6% (up 0.3pp), showing aggressive competition for longer-term deposits.

medium.title: Experts: Securities Market Next Week Could Fall to 1,700 Point Level
medium.summary: Vietnam's stock market experienced extreme volatility in early March due to Middle East tensions. VN-Index fell 112.49 points (-5.98%) to 1,767.84 points despite 50% higher trading volume. Analysts warn of continued pressure from foreign selling (over 6,000 billion VND net selling) despite upcoming FTSE Russell upgrade consideration.

medium.title: Over 1.2 Trillion VND on Vietnam Stock Market Held by Foreign Investors: Awaiting Upgrade Breakthrough
medium.summary: Despite continuous net selling since 2023 (260,000 billion VND on HoSE alone), foreign investors still hold over 1.2 trillion VND market cap in Vietnamese stocks (12% of total). About 30% of global emerging market funds and nearly 40% of Asian investment funds hold Vietnamese stocks, indicating strong institutional presence awaiting the September 2026 market upgrade.

medium.title: Largest Private Bank in System Just Increased Savings Interest Rate to 7% Range
medium.summary: VPBank has adjusted its deposit rate schedule from March 10, 2026, with the highest rate now at 7% annually for 12-month online deposits. Short-term rates (1-5 months) remain at the regulatory ceiling of 4.75%, while medium-term rates increased by 0.1pp to 6.6-6.9% for online channels.

medium.title: Banks Spend Over 132,000 Billion for Employees: BIDV, VietinBank, Vietcombank, MB and VPBank Lead
medium.summary: Employee costs across 27 listed banks reached over 132,400 billion VND in 2025, up about 10% year-on-year. This reflects banks' expansion activities, digital transformation investments, and talent competition in the increasingly competitive financial labor market.
